correctness.rationale: For every admissible parameter array, conditional on the entire driving-sign path the per-time environment rows give independent bounded signs. The exact Lucas parity identity yields mean magnitude at most (1-2 epsilon) raised to 2^popcount(S_n). Binary-digit sparsity plus the independent geometric holding-time representation imply a pathwise N^{o(1)} total conditional mean and squared mean. The conditional variance sum is N-o(N); Kolmogorov's nonidentical independent bounded-increment LIL gives both sharp endpoints. Fubini transfers this to almost every fixed environment, and the predictable covariance bracket plus bounded-jump martingale functional CLT yields the quenched independent planar Brownian limit. Exact finite checks of the cardinality-folding and conditional means passed 12,002 assertions; these checks are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact source paper arXiv:2610.01658v1, Corollary 9 and adjacent remark, proves only annealed normality under independently resampled time levels and expressly identifies quenched normality as unresolved. The presented law of the iterated logarithm supplies the missing almost-sure quenched bracket control with a sharp constant. Its Section 3 theorem uses independent subset coefficients, while the cardinality-grouped model identifies multiple subset coefficients and therefore violates that hypothesis. The older arXiv:2010.16000 is an if-and-only-if criterion rather than a verification for these random one-factor environments. Targeted title, alias and implication searches and a comparison with relevant accessible previous claims found no directly covering theorem; this is a bounded best-knowledge priority assessment.

value.rationale: The primary 2026 paper proves only annealed normality for this exact natural one-factor independent-time environment and explicitly identifies quenched normality as unresolved. The new result closes that mathematically motivated gap under the full uniform-ellipticity assumptions and computes a sharp two-sided iterated-logarithm envelope for predictable cross-variation. This is stronger than a routine expectation or variance computation, and the binary-digit sparsity mechanism is structurally specific to cardinality grouping.
